body:
The two schools combine cleanly. **Fundamentals decide what, Stage 2 decides when, the stop decides how much.** CAN SLIM, SEPA and Darvas's "techno-fundamentalism" were all designed this way ([AAII](https://www.aaii.com/journal/article/william-oneil-can-slim-approach-to-selecting-growth-stocks); [Chartmill](https://www.chartmill.com/documentation/trading-and-investing/methodologies/523-SEPA-Explained-Mark-Minervinis-Specific-Entry-Point-Analysis-System)). A long-term investor does not need to be a swing trader to use this. Simply refusing to add new money to a high-quality stock while it is in a Weinstein Stage 4 decline avoids many "right company, terrible timing" years, like Radico in 2008.

`case_study:costco-2009-2026` · tickers US-COST · confidence: verified

Costco's ~14-15% markup cap and membership fees (which are most of operating profit) create a low-price, high-trust flywheel; renewal rates ~90% US/Canada. March 2009 low ~$38 [unverified] -> all-time high $1,094.32 (May 2026): ~29x plus special dividends ($5 2015, $7 2017, $10 2020, $15 2024) [unverified]. Split [approx]: EPS ~$2.5 (FY09) -> ~$18 (FY25) ≈ 7x; P/E ~15x -> ~48-60x ≈ 3.5x. Feb 2025 P/E ~60x was the highest in its history (prior record 56.4x in Apr 1999, after which the stock fell >20% in months; Aug 2026 trailing ~48x). Drawdowns: ~-50% 2007-09 and after the 1999 valuation peak [unverified]. EARLY SIGNAL (always visible): rising paid members, renewal rates, fee increases every ~5-6 years with no churn, comparable sales beating peers through recessions. Who caught it: Charlie Munger (Costco director from 1997, lifelong holder and public advocate); Berkshire held Costco ~2000-2020 and sold in 2020 near ~$300 [from memory, unverified], missing ~3.5x. Stall: by 2025-26 growth ~high single digit at ~50x earnings — commentators flag 'very light growth' for the price. LESSON: a capital-light-ish customer-aligned model compounds EPS steadily; the last decade's extra return came from the market paying up for certainty, which is a non-repeatable tailwind and a risk.

- **Start → end:** ~$38 (Mar 2009) [unverified] → $1,094.32 ATH (May 2026) (~29x + special divs)
- **EPS vs rerating:** EPS ~7x, P/E ~3.5x
- **Max drawdown:** ~-50% (2007-09) [unverified]
- **Early signal:** member count, ~90% renewals, fee hikes without churn
- **Who caught it:** Charlie Munger (director since 1997)
- **Ended/stalled:** not ended; valuation 48-60x
- **Lesson:** steady EPS + rerating tailwind; Berkshire sold too early

`person:chuck-akre` | confidence: **single-source** | tags: us, process, quality, compounding, low-turnover

Akre Capital Management; ran FBR Focus Fund, then the Akre Focus Fund from 2009 (John Neff and Chris Cerrone later took over; Akre stepped back from the strategy around 2020). Returns: compounded over ~13% a year since 2009 (Quartr) and top-third rankings vs peers for years; a Substack figure of 15.44% vs 14.22% for the S&P 500 is unverified; Q4 2024 -0.41% vs +2.41% for the S&P. Process edge: the 'three-legged stool' - (1) an extraordinary business with high returns on owners' capital, (2) talented management with integrity who treat shareholders as partners, (3) a long runway to reinvest free cash flow at high returns. When all three exist it is a 'compounding machine' and the job is to sit still. Signature long holds: American Tower, Mastercard, Moody's, O'Reilly Automotive, later KKR and Constellation Software. Structural edge: patient capital and very low turnover, small team. Mistakes: low turnover means sitting through valuation compression (2022 drawdown) and occasional late exits from businesses whose reinvestment runway faded (unverified specifics). Copyable: the three questions are a direct checklist for Indian compounders (e.g., ROE >20%, honest promoter, reinvestment runway); hold winners; measure in 5-year blocks.

Run top to bottom. Each line names its mandatory output. Details are in the sections below.

| Step | Do | Mandatory output |
|---|---|---|
| S0 Selection (live dives) | Seeded random draw from a written frame; skip rules fixed before the frame is built | Seed(s), frame counts, ordered skip log with reasons; entity exists through the call horizon |
| Rule zero | Edge question | 3 lines (consensus, key variable, layer) |
| S2 | Every disqualifier-v2 rule, dated source | pass / fail / unknown table, before L1 |
| Stage 3 | PEAD quintile + event date; credibility vs peer median (or, no concalls, AR-mode asset table + disclosure flags) | Signal block for the card |
| L1 Map | Unit by business type; peers. **Flag non-operating stakes and cyclicality here** | Value chain; holdco / cyclical flags |
| L2 Financials | 10-yr re-derivation; concentration; core PBT. **Cyclicals: normalised EPS and peak-cycle test** | Re-derived tables; trailing vs normalised P/E |
| L3 Units | Unit P&L, payback two ways | Unit table |
| L4 Costs | Rank by weight; top-3 in physical terms; materials ratio by quarter (manufacturers) | Cost-driver table with bps sensitivity |
| L5 Governance | RPT table; parent-take table; **fees/royalties followed to the parent; vote results**; ownership supply | RPT + parent-take + vote-result tables |
| L6 Scuttlebutt | Hypothesis-led site list | Surprises-vs-model list |
| L7 Synthesis | Override table incl. "looks good" flags; **holdco discount causes** | Open-flag count; variant view or size 0 |
| L8 Valuation + decision | Worksheet v1.3 (cash tax, ROIIC realism, exit-bet table, non-op stakes, normalised base) + card v1.2 (survival cap, tail anchoring) | Worksheet, card, paper calls (live: ingested) |
| Close | Method lessons + open items; memdb seed | "What the method taught"; analysis record (no verdict on method tests) |
